test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 01 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: By selling an article for ₹19, a dealer makes a profit of 20%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 40%?
solution:
**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹19

Profit = 20%

New Profit = 40%

**Formula used:**

Cost Price (CP) = dfrac{SP}{1 + (Profit)/(100)}

New Selling Price (NSP) = (1 + (New Profit)/(100)) times CP

**Calculation:**

CP = dfrac{19}{1 + (20)/(100)}

⇒ CP = dfrac{19}{1.20}

⇒ CP = ₹15.83

NSP = (1 + (40)/(100)) times 15.83

⇒ NSP = (1.40) times 15.83

⇒ NSP = ₹22.16

Increase in Selling Price = NSP - SP

⇒ Increase in Selling Price = ₹22.16 - ₹19

⇒ Increase in Selling Price = ₹3.17

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**
